implementation_notes: The classic Java realization is an abstract class (or interface) Component declaring the uniform operation, leaf classes implementing it, and a container holding List<Component> whose implementation iterates the children and combines their results. Put child management on the container class and reach it through a cast or an isComposite() predicate, because declaring add()/remove() on Component forces leaves into no-op or throwing stubs and forfeits the substitutability the pattern is supposed to provide. The JDK already ships instances of the structure - javax.swing.text.Element (getElementCount/getElement/isLeaf) and org.w3c.dom.Node - so check the platform tree before writing a new hierarchy.
pitfalls: Child management declared on Component makes every leaf carry meaningless add/remove methods; keep it on the container and pay one checked cast.
List<Component>.remove uses equals, so node identity must be decided deliberately (default identity vs a records-style equals).
Deep recursion overflows the stack on large or adversarial trees; iterative traversal with an explicit Deque is the escape.

variants.name: Sealed interface + records with exhaustive switch (Java 17/21)
variants.idiom_name: sealed interface Node + record variants + exhaustive switch
variants.implementation_notes: Java 21 can express the node set as a sealed interface whose record variants are fixed by the permits clause; the recursive operation becomes an external method with a switch over the sealed type, and the compiler enforces exhaustiveness because it knows every permitted subtype (JEP 409 plus JEP 441). Nodes become immutable records, so an edit rebuilds the spine of the tree instead of mutating a child list. Choose this when the node set is closed and owned by you; keep the abstract-class variant when other teams must add node kinds or when the runtime is older than 17.
pitfalls: Exhaustiveness holds only while the hierarchy stays sealed in the same module and package; an unsealed extension point breaks the guarantee silently.
Do not add a default branch to quiet the compiler - the compile error on a new node kind is the entire value of the sealed switch.
Records with collection components are only shallowly immutable: the List can still be mutated unless it is copied or wrapped on construction.
